wal: analyse what makes a piece of writing effective and build our success criteria for the final write
tib: Understanding exactly what a writer is doing and why helps me make deliberate, purposeful choices in my own writing.
isb: annotating the model text for four features and recording the success criteria I will use for my final narrative.

title: Grammar Warm-Up
subtitle: Which feature? Match each sentence to the writing technique it shows.

cards.label: Sentence A
lines: The smell hit him like a wall:
oil, rot and something sharp.
Simile? Power of three? Fronted adverbial?

cards.label: Sentence B
lines: Trembling with cold, he crept
to the edge of the step.
Simile? Fronted adverbial? Hyperbole?

cards.label: Sentence C
lines: Although he did not know her name,
Varjak felt something settle inside him.
Alliteration? Power of three? Complex sentence?

title: Introducing the model text
lines: This week you have practised all the skills
you will need for your final narrative:
• Simile and alliteration
• Hyperbole and the power of three
• Fronted adverbials
• Subordinating conjunctions
• Speech punctuation
The model text brings all of these together.
Listen carefully. What do you notice?

label: Read aloud the model text. Pupils follow on their printed copy.

title: Annotation key
left_label: What to look for (use four colours)
right_lines: Annotating forces you to slow down
and notice what the writer is doing.
Every choice in the model text is
When you annotate, you are building
a toolkit you can borrow from
A good reader is always also
a reader who is learning to write.

lines: Annotate the model text with your partner.
Use the four colours from the annotation key.
Work through the text paragraph by paragraph.
When you have finished, discuss:
• Which feature appears most often?
• Which moment in the text did you find
most effective, and why?
• What will you borrow for your own writing?
Be ready to share one observation with the class.

title: Building our success criteria
lines: Based on the model text, what must your
final narrative include?
Let’s build the success criteria together.
For each criterion, we need to know:
• What it is
• What it looks like in writing
Record the success criteria in your books.
You will use these as a checklist
throughout the Challenge phase.

q1: Which feature in the model text surprised you most, and why?
q2: What is one specific thing from the model text that you want to use in your narrative?
q3: Which success criterion do you think will be the hardest to achieve in your own writing?
